title: Focused chough next, a verification guard before build, and done-stage resume
description: Focused chough next, a verification guard before build, and done-stage resume
acceptance_criteria: Focused next: `chough next` stops sharing the status report and prints a compact action view: the objective; the current stage with its status, iteration and side-stage callers; the recorded native change with the native read state, summary state, approval_valid, correction_valid, terminal evidence validity, native next action and the approved-delta result (REQ-cli-022); the next valid action with its reason and, when one applies, the command to run; the gate for the next main stage with its label; open awaiting-human gates; checkpoint blockers; open acceptance-blocking bug IDs and the count of other open bugs; and only the observations that are referenced and not current (historical, pruned or unavailable), each with its ID, label and at most three referencing records, at most 10 listed beside their total, plus the counts of referenced current observations and of unreferenced observations. It prints no raw native output, no observation records, no snapshot and no full reference list, and names `chough status` as the full view. Text is the default and `--json` prints the same fields as compact JSON with schema_version 1 and view `next`. Each form is at most 16384 bytes: every list shows at most 10 entries with its total, every string taken from a record is cut to at most 512 bytes with a visible marker, and if the result would still exceed the cap, list entries are dropped until it fits and `truncated` is true. `chough status` stays the full view with unchanged fields; its `--help` says it always prints JSON. Both commands compute next_valid_action with one shared function, so they report the same action for the same records, and each makes at most one `specsync change status` read and evaluates the stage gate on that same response. A fixture with 500 referenced stale observations, 40 awaiting-human gates and 40 blockers of 4 KiB each, and a native response near the parse bound keeps both forms within 16384 bytes with correct totals; a counting stub shows one native read per command; the pull request reports both forms' byte counts on this repository (LIFE-3, FLOW-13, LIFE-7, REQ-cli-003, REQ-cli-021).

Done-stage resume: in stage done, active and with no awaiting-human gate, when the recorded native change is archived with authenticated terminal evidence or no native change is recorded, the next valid action no longer echoes the checkpoint's next_action. It says the cycle is closed and recommends a new one: `chough stage reset --to intent --reason "<why>"` (or `--to plan` when the approved intent already covers the new work), then `specsync change new "<outcome>" --spec <module> --path <path>`, then `chough checkpoint --native-change <id> --next-action "<next step>"`; when native status names a next action, such as merging a pull request that is still open, the view shows it as the thing to check first. Every reset command Chough suggests carries `--reason`. An archive whose terminal evidence does not authenticate keeps today's gate refusal. `chough stage reset` replaces the checkpoint's next_action with `New cycle from <stage> after reset: <reason>. Create or record the native change (specsync change new, then chough checkpoint --native-change <id>) and set the next action.`, so a stale action is not carried into the new cycle; `chough stage back` leaves next_action unchanged, and the transition records the reason as before. The canonical skill's references/checkpoint.md gives the same steps with `--reason`. Tests drive a done fixture with an archived stub change: the action text and reason, that the suggested reset with its placeholder filled succeeds, and the replaced next_action afterwards (FLOW-13, LIFE-3, FLOW-2, REQ-cli-021).

Approved-delta guard: when a move to build, test or accept (by advance, skip, back or reset) meets a native change in state approved, implementing or verifying whose status reports approval_valid true, Chough also checks that the semantic deltas are the ones approved instead of trusting approval_valid alone (BUG-0002: SpecSync 6.1.1 keeps it true after an approved delta is edited). It reads `.specsync/changes/<id>/approvals.json` read-only, bounded at 4 MiB (SpecSync 6.1.1's own change-artifact bound; the record bound of 64 KiB is too small for ledgers that SpecSync itself has grown past 270 KB), takes the last definition approval as SpecSync does, and compares its approved_delta_digests with digests it computes with SpecSync 6.1.1's framing (SHA-256 over the length-framed domain `specsync.approved-delta.v1`, the module name and the delta body with CRLF normalized to LF) for every module in the status response's change.affected_specs, each delta read under the same 4 MiB bound. A module whose digest differs, whose delta is missing, or that is affected but absent from the approval refuses the move with `refused:native-delta-changed`, naming the modules and the next native actions: restore the approved delta, or get a new human scope approval (`specsync change approve <id> --actor "<their name>"`) and then run `specsync change check <id>`. When the comparison cannot be made (the ledger is missing, unreadable, over the bound or malformed; there is no definition approval; a change with deltas has an approval without approved_delta_digests; status reports no affected_specs; a delta cannot be read) the move is refused with `refused:native-delta-unverifiable`, the reason and the next native action `specsync change status <id>`. A no_spec_change approval with an empty digest map passes. The guard starts no process: native reads stay the one bounded `specsync change status` read, no gate runs `specsync change check`, and archived changes keep the terminal-evidence rule. The gate and native summary in `chough next` and `chough status` show the result. Tests: digests computed for this repository's archived changes match their recorded approvals; an edited delta, an added module, a deleted delta, a missing ledger, an approval without digests and an oversized ledger each give the stated label, and the refused move leaves the session and transitions byte-identical; a CRLF-only edit and an unchanged approval pass (FLOW-5, LIFE-7, LIFE-1, REQ-cli-008, REQ-cli-022).

Host wording: the canonical SKILL.md host section, README.md and docs/integrations.md say that `--host openai`, the default, writes `.agents/skills`, a shared skills directory, and that Google Antigravity read the skill from that directory in one observed run reported narratively in closed PR #20 and not independently verified; that `--host gemini` writes `.gemini/skills`, which no run has exercised; and nothing about Gemini CLI. The host map in src/skill.rs and `chough skill status` are unchanged: status reports `.agents/skills` once, as the openai directory, and does not count it for gemini. KNOWN_PREVIOUS lists the origin/main digests of each bundle file this change edits (SKILL.md and references/checkpoint.md), so unedited earlier copies read known-outdated and update while edited copies stay edited; Chough's own .agents/ and .claude/ copies are refreshed and read current, and no bundle file gains U+2013 or U+2014 (FLOW-1, LIFE-4, REQ-cli-016, REQ-cli-019).

Cold-start record: docs/exercises/cold-start.md gains a section dated 2026-11-01 for Google Antigravity, marked unverified and narrative only, whose assessment table cites the closed PR #20 log (`.chough/artifacts/gemini-cold-start.log` at commit 53b60aa on branch gemini/feat/gemini-host-cold-start) as its only source and says what that source cannot show: it was written by the agent itself with no event log or transcript, it names the model inconsistently (Gemini 3.8 Flash High in the log, Gemini 2.5 Pro in the PR's own document), and its change was closed unmerged. Its done-stage friction is cited as the finding this change fixes. docs/integrations.md gets an Antigravity row with the same caveat. The earlier Codex record is not rewritten (FLOW-13, LIFE-4).

Guidance and verification: docs/cli.md documents the next view (fields, text default and `--json`, the 16384-byte cap, one native read), status as the full view, both refusal labels with their next actions and the reset next_action replacement; docs/architecture.md says the guard reads the native approval ledger read-only and copies nothing; the README quick start shows `chough next`; examples/feature-bug-loop.sh and examples/visual-design.sh read `chough next --json`; existing tests that read full status fields through `next --json` read `status` instead. Cases TC-cli-0120 to TC-cli-0124 cover the cap, done-stage resume, the reset next_action, a changed delta and an unverifiable delta; they link REQ-cli-021 and REQ-cli-022, so they are added and run after the scoped `change check` materializes them. BUG-0002 stays open with a note that Chough now guards it; it closes when CI pins a SpecSync release that reports an edited approved delta. The full suite, `fledge lanes run verify` (including the feature-and-bug exercise) and native structural checks pass on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows CI. No new integration, model client, storage or record kind (LIFE-6, LIFE-7, FLOW-7).

answers.constraints: specs/cli/context.md lessons: SpecSync 6.1.1 keeps approval_valid true after an approved delta is edited, so rely on more than status (BUG-0002); change check refuses while tasks.md has unchecked boxes, so human gates and post-verification steps are plain text; REQ IDs added by a delta validate only after change check materializes them, so cases for REQ-cli-021 and REQ-cli-022 are added after the scoped check; pub(super), not pub(crate); disposable repositories need a local Git identity; Claude Code discovered .claude/skills and not .agents/skills. Measured on this repository with specsync 6.1.1: change check without --commit is not read-only (it materializes canonical specs and writes verification, verification-attempts, state and change.md even when verification fails), refuses with exit 1 for unchecked tasks, an edited delta and failed verification alike, and runs verification commands, so no gate may run it. Invariants: native state is read and never copied, inputs are bounded, unknown stays unknown and refuses gated moves, no approval or review is recorded or inferred. AGENTS.md: no new integration, model client, storage or record kind; .chough/ is not an affected path. Open PR #22 also modifies REQ-cli-008, REQ-cli-016 and REQ-cli-019 and edits SKILL.md, references/checkpoint.md and KNOWN_PREVIOUS, so this change adds requirements rather than modifying those, and whichever merges second rebases its KNOWN_PREVIOUS lines.
